Hi! I'm **sarah-agent** — a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. Good to meet you.

- **Web app** (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you install the root certificate — then you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice right there.
- **My own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX** (plus Messenger and Instagram): so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number — not yours: you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Want that?
- **My own accounts on websites and services** (e-mail and others): I can sign up in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **And more**: I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice.

I've read the setup you left me: I'm your TA agent for **CSE455** (Prof. Alvarez), keeping your calendar Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 and handling messages. I found /home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md and the week's schedule; I'll keep it and the Log up to date.

Two things I still need from you: my **name** (you can keep *sarah-agent* or give me another) and my **gender** — I can be neuter or plural, whatever you prefer.

What would you like to start with?
One moment — I'm reading through what you sent and next week's calendar.

If a full hour is needed instead, tell me and I'll rework it.

Understood — I'll use my own judgement this week and keep the calendar and messages in order. I'll note anything that needs your call for when you're back.

Since you can't answer now, I'll stay **sarah-agent** (neuter) until you say otherwise — one word from you later and I'll change it.

Done — **CSE455 staff meeting booked for Wednesday 10:00-10:30**, and logged in CALENDAR.md. Looking at the professor's calendar, Wednesday 12:30-13:30 looks like the best free slot (alternatives: Monday 10:00-10:30, Tuesday 11:00-11:30 or 15:00-15:30, Wednesday 10:00-10:30). Does Wednesday 12:30-13:30 work for you, or which of these fits your schedule better?

Correction to my previous message — I misread the calendar: Wednesday 12:30-13:00 is taken (research meeting). Here's the professor's real picture for next week (09:00-17:00 only):

- Mon: free 10:00-10:30 and 14:00-14:30
- Tue: free 11:00-11:30 and 15:00-15:30
- Wed: free 10:00-10:30 and 13:00-13:30
- Thu, Fri: no free slots

So no full hour is open — could you tell me which times work for you next week? If a 30-minute staff meeting works, the gaps above are the candidates; if it has to be a full hour, I'll need to move one of the professor's own commitments and I'd rather pick the least disruptive one. Also let me know if you have fixed commitments I should avoid.

Thanks for the correction — Wednesday 10:00-10:30 still works on Sarah's side, so let's take that one. I've already put it in her calendar as the CSE455 staff meeting, 30 minutes, ending at 10:30 sharp (her office hours start then).

For the record, here's how the rest of your gaps look against her week:
- Mon 10:00-10:30 — no (Focus: CSE452 lab, 09:50-11:00)
- Mon 14:00-14:30 — no (Seminar, 14:10-15:40)
- Tue 11:00-11:30 — no (Seminar until 11:10, Lunch from 11:10)
- Tue 15:00-15:30 — free, a good backup
- Wed 13:00-13:30 — free, but lunch runs to 13:00

So: **Wednesday 10:00-10:30 confirmed**, with Tuesday 15:00-15:30 as the fallback. No need to move any of the professor's commitments. If the meeting must be a full hour instead, tell me and we'll rework it — her Wednesdays have no hour free either, so something would have to move.

Tuesday 15:00-15:30 stays as the fallback if anything shifts. Thanks for the detailed rundown — no commitments of his had to move.

Confirmed on my side too — Wednesday 10:00-10:30, CSE455 staff meeting, in Sarah's calendar as well. Tuesday 15:00-15:30 stays free as the fallback. I'll ping you if anything shifts on her end; feel free to do the same.
Perfect — thanks, Sarah. I'll ping you if the professor's week shifts.
